subject: Post-call exec recap: AuroraTech discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@auroratech.com>, Claire Donovan <claire.donovan@auroratech.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call exec recap: AuroraTech discovery & next steps

Hi Sanjay / Claire,

Thanks again for taking the time today — I appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps for your exec/ procurement review.

High-level business outcomes you described:
- Reduce time-to-insight for customer support transcripts from ~24h to near real-time (target: <5 mins)
- Cut annotation/triage costs tied to manual categorization by ~60% in year 1
- Improve CSAT on escalations by surfacing intent & severity at intake

Top pain points we heard:
- Current on-prem pipeline batches transcripts nightly; SLA misses when volume spikes
- Inability to route high-severity cases quickly because signals are buried in attachments/notes
- Cost unpredictability for peak seasonal loads (Q4)

Goals / success criteria you called out:
- Proof-of-value within 6-8 weeks for a single region/queue
- Demonstrable latency improvement and cost baseline vs current infra
- Executive alignment on procurement path and a committed pilot budget for POC

Technical scope we covered:
- Small pilot (1 queue, ~50k messages/day) -> Redwood hosted or Dedicated evaluation
- Need for KV caching of customer history + prefix caching for low-latency rerank
- Data control: logs + audit required, will support customer-managed KMS for production

Next steps / asks (owner / ETA):
1) Marissa (us) -> Share Mutual Action Plan + MVP requirements (attached) — today
2) Sanjay (AuroraTech) -> Confirm pilot owner, procurement contact, and preferred billing model (SOW vs committed capacity) — by Wed 7/15
3) Aditya (SE) -> Share proposed topology and telemetry checklist for pilot — by Tue 7/14
4) Schedule a 30-min exec sync (Marissa + Vivek + Aurora exec sponsor) if Aurora wants pricing flexibility — tentatively week of 7/20

Attachments: AuroraTech_MVP_requirements.pdf, Redwood_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (MAP has proposed timeline, milestones, success metrics, and tentative pricing bands).

Open items / risks noted:
- Procurement runway: if procurement requires an RFP + security review, timeline may extend beyond target POC window.
- Data gravity: if full workload needs to stay on-prem, Dedicated or Private deployment will change cost and ops assumptions.

If this looks right I'll loop in legal/procurement at your signal and lock in the pilot SLA / kickoff date.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the comprehensive recap. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Exec sponsor: Vivian Park (SVP Customer Experience) will be the final approver for any pilot spend >$50k; I will loop her in once we have a firm MAP and a pilot cost estimate.
2) Procurement: procurement@auroratech.com is the right contact for commercial terms. They typically ask for a data processing addendum and SOC 2 evidence up front.
3) Timeline constraint: we need the POC to deliver metrics before our Q3 board review (target completion 8/28). If procurement pushes an RFP, that could slip.

Action for you: please include an estimate range for Hosted vs Dedicated for the pilot (monthly) in the MAP. Also include the minimum data handling controls and an expected SOC2 delivery/attestation window.

I'll get procurement and Vivian on a brief email once we have the updated MAP.

Sanjay

Hi Sanjay / Claire,

Quick technical notes from our conversation and an initial checklist for the pilot topology. Attaching a 1-pager telemetry checklist as well — happy to convert to your format.

Key technical clarifications:
- Pilot topology: recommended Redwood Dedicated (single-region reserved pool) for predictable latency; Hosted can work for eval but we recommend Dedicated if you want consistent <5min latency under spikes.
- Data ingress: we support S3-backed ingestion or direct TLS endpoints; for PII-sensitive queues we recommend S3 + customer-managed KMS.
- KV cache: will need a warm-up policy (we suggested 12-24h pre-warming for top 10% of customers) to meet tail latency SLOs.

Telemetry checklist attached: key metrics we will collect during pilot (latency p50/p95/p99, token costs, model fallback counts, error rates, routing logs).

I'll coordinate with Marissa on finalizing the MAP and a pilot topology diagram.

Thanks,

Subject: Exec recap & ask: AuroraTech pilot — business outcomes, risks, and pricing path

Hi Sanjay / Claire — copying Marissa and Aditya. I wanted to summarize at an exec level and outline the asks we need from AuroraTech to accelerate the pilot.

Business outcomes we will target (pilot):
- Demonstrate median latency improvement from batch to <60s for routed escalations
- Reduce manual triage spend on pilot queue by 50% (measured by agent-hours)
- Provide clear cost baseline and expected per-ticket unit economics for Q4 planning

Primary risks to call out:
- Procurement runway: if procurement requires an RFP + multi-vendor security tests, pilot start may slip past board date.
- Data residency: if pilot scope expands to on-prem workloads, Dedicated/Private pricing and timeline change materially.

Pricing / procurement path (our recommendation):
1) Pilot on Dedicated reserved monthly capacity for predictability (we can size a 2-3 week ramp).
2) If Aurora commits to a 12-month reserved commit after pilot, we can consider a limited pilot credit / one-time onboarding discount.
3) For procurement: we will provide SOC2 report and DPA; legal commercial redlines are acceptable but need to be scoped early.

Executive ask:
- Sanjay / Vivian: confirm pilot owner and procurement contact (procurement@auroratech.com is listed) and confirm whether Aurora will require an RFP or if a direct SOW is acceptable.
- Aurora: confirm desired pilot completion target (your board date 8/28 noted) so we can align resources.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 15-minute exec touchpoint this week to align on procurement gating items. We're prepared to escalate pricing approvals internally if Aurora confirms pilot ROI and a likely commit band.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
